topIssues.title: blob-archiver does not support /eth/v1/beacon/blobs/ endpoint, breaking beacon fallback
topIssues.author: karlfloersch
topIssues.body:
## Summary

The blob-archiver does not implement the `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/<slot>` endpoint, which is the current beacon API endpoint used by `op-node` and `op-supernode` for fetching blobs. It only serves the older `/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/<slot>` endpoint.

When `L1BeaconClient` rotates to the blob-archiver as a fallback (via `--l1.beacon-archiver`), the client calls `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/` which doesn't exist on the archiver — the request hits an unregistered route and returns a malformed response (bare JSON array instead of `{"data": [...]}`).

This affects both **op-node** and **op-supernode** since they share the same `BeaconHTTPClient`.

## Endpoint Support Matrix

| Endpoint | Beacon Proxy | Blob Archiver | QuickNode |
|----------|-------------|---------------|-----------|
| `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/` (current) | works | **not implemented** | works |
| `/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/` (old) | works | works | works |

## Root Cause

The beacon API transitioned from `/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/` to `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/`. The op-node client was updated to use the new `/blobs/` endpoint ([op-service/sources/l1_beacon_client.go](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-service/sources/l1_beacon_client.go#L28)), but the blob-archiver was never updated to serve it.

In the [blob-archiver source](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/blob-archiver/blob/master/api/service/api.go#L109), only the old endpoint is registered:
```go
r.Get("/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/{id}", result.blobSidecarHandler)
// missing: r.Get("/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/{id}", result.blobsHandler)
```

## Response Format Differences

The two endpoints return different response formats:

**`/blobs/` (current)** — returns raw blobs:
```json
{"data": ["0x<hex blob>", "0x<hex blob>", ...]}
```

**`/blob_sidecars/` (old)** — returns sidecar objects:
```json
{"data": [{"index": "0", "blob": "0x...", "kzg_commitment": "0x...", ...}]}
```

The client deserializes into `APIBeaconBlobsResponse{Data []*Blob}` which expects the `/blobs/` format.

## Impact

- `--l1.beacon-archiver` / `--l1.beacon-fallbacks` is broken when pointing to the blob-archiver
- Only affects cases where the primary beacon can't serve blobs (e.g. PeerDAS nodes for old slots, expired blobs)
- Discovered during supernode canary testing on interop-v0

## Fix

The blob-archiver needs to add a handler for `/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/{id}` that returns the raw blob format `{"data": ["0x...", ...]}`.

topPRs.title: Chore/public docs migration
topPRs.author: ZakAyesh
topPRs.body:
**Description**
Migrates all content from ethereum-optimism/docs into the monorepo at docs/public-docs/. This is a verbatim move with no content edits — Mintlify remains the docs framework, just pointed at the new location. The live site at docs.optimism.io and all 500+ redirects remain unchanged. After this PR merges, we'll do the Mintlify dashboard cutover, triage open issues/PRs in the old repo, and archive ethereum-optimism/docs.

**Tests**
No automated tests for this change. Correctness will be verified manually after the Mintlify dashboard cutover by confirming docs.optimism.io resolves correctly and spot-checking a sample of redirects.

**Additional context**
This consolidation means doc updates and their corresponding code changes can be reviewed atomically in a single PR, rather than requiring separate PRs across two repos. It also places docs directly alongside the code they describe, making it easier to catch and fix stale documentation. The existing docs/ directory (audits, postmortems) is untouched.

topPRs.title: interop: add strong consistency guarantees
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19420

## Summary

This PR refactors the supernode interop activity around a single persisted transition model so that normal execution and crash recovery use the same apply path.

For a new reader, the important mental model is:

1. `progressAndRecord()` is the top-level interop tick.
2. If a `PendingTransition` already exists in `VerifiedDB`, interop replays it.
3. Otherwise interop observes the world, verifies the next timestamp, builds a `PendingTransition`, persists it, and applies it immediately.
4. The transition stays in the WAL until all of its side effects succeed.

This is the minimal-diff version of the stronger consistency work: it keeps the existing package structure, but makes the state transitions explicit and replayable.

Context: this work is informed by the Runtime Verification audit writeup here:
- https://github.com/runtimeverification/_audits_Ethereum-optimism_optimism_interopv2/issues/8

## What Changed

### 1. Unified normal execution and recovery

Interop no longer has separate "normal apply" and "startup recovery" logic for the important state transitions.

Instead, effectful decisions are represented as a generic `PendingTransition` stored in `VerifiedDB`, and both steady-state execution and restart recovery go through the same `applyPendingTransition()` path.

This covers:
- `DecisionAdvance`
- `DecisionInvalidate`
- `DecisionRewind`

### 2. Verification is now read-only

`verify()` no longer mutates `logsDB` while deciding whether a frontier is valid.

Instead:
- frontier verification uses an in-memory `frontierView`
- accepted-history lookups still come from `logsDB`
- frontier logs are only persisted later, during `DecisionAdvance` transition apply

That makes the WAL the real boundary for stateful changes.

### 3. Advance / invalidate / rewind are explicit transition kinds

`buildPendingTransition()` now constructs explicit transition payloads.

Notably:
- rewind uses an explicit `RewindPlan`
- advance persists exact frontier blocks during apply
- invalidation preserves the WAL until all invalidation side effects succeed

### 4. Replays are idempotent where they need to be

To support "persist first, clear last":
- `VerifiedDB.Commit()` is idempotent for exact duplicate replays
- rewind apply reports all failures, but keeps the WAL until the transition converges
- invalidation and rewind failures preserve the transition for retry
- invalid rewind WAL state now fails closed instead of being silently cleared

### 5. Top-level interop flow is easier to read again

The orchestration is back to a simpler shape:
- `progressAndRecord()` owns the transition lifecycle
- `progressInterop()` computes the next action
- `checkPreconditions()` gates verification
- `decideVerifiedResult()` interprets verification output

Dead wrappers and stale helper paths were removed along the way.

### 6. Reset callbacks are no longer part of interop correctness

Interop now treats `Reset()` as a no-op interface shim. The actual correctness path is the persisted transition apply logic.

The broader chain-container rewind/invalidation APIs are still powerful footguns, so this PR adds explicit comments/TODOs documenting that they should only be used from interop transition application until that interface is narrowed further.

### 7. Small cleanup and reviewability improvements

Also included in this branch:
- removed dead denylist clearing APIs (`ClearDenied`, `DenyList.Clear`)
- removed dead helpers/wrappers (`loadLogs`, `rewindAccepted`, `RewindAfter`, etc.)
- clarified the logsDB warning for chains with block times greater than one second
- cleaned up stale comments and compatibility artifacts

## Current Top-Level Flow

```text
Start
  -> progressAndRecord
     -> if pending transition exists:
          applyPendingTransition
     -> else:
          progressInterop
            -> observeRound
            -> checkPreconditions
            -> verify
            -> decideVerifiedResult
          -> if wait (DecisionWait):
               refreshCurrentL1OnWait
          -> if rewind with no prior verified state:
               return early (nothing to rewind)
          -> else (advance, invalidate, or rewind):
               buildPendingTransition
               SetPendingTransition
               applyPendingTransition
```

## Follow-Up

A follow-up PR should remove the ability to trigger rewinds/reorg side effects from outside interop until cross-activity concurrency between these stateful operations is fully designed and enforced.

Today the code documents those APIs as dangerous footguns, but the safer end state is to narrow that surface so interop transition application is the only place allowed to drive rewinds.

## Why This Is Better

Compared with `develop`, this branch moves the interop activity closer to an explicit transaction model:
- decisions are separated from side effects
- recovery and steady-state share the same apply path
- frontier verification no longer mutates durable state
- WAL clearing happens only after the transition has been applied

That makes the database/control-flow behavior much easier to review in one place.

Just as importantly, the consistency checks (L1 fork verification, accepted snapshot re-verification, stale logsDB detection) ensure that each virtual node's local data is internally consistent before interop cross-validates across chains. This means cross-validation only ever operates on trustworthy inputs.

## Files To Read First

If you are new to this diff, start here:
- `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/interop.go`
- `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/verified_db.go`
- `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/logdb.go`
- `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/verification_view.go`
- `op-supernode/supernode/chain_container/invalidation.go`

## Test Plan

Rerun coverage I checked while updating this branch:
- [x] `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop/... -count=1`
- [x] `go test ./op-supernode/supernode/activity/superroot -count=1`

Focused regressions added/updated on this branch include:
- pending advance replay after commit succeeds idempotently
- pending invalidate/rewind transitions are preserved on failure
- rewind apply reports all failures
- invalid rewind WAL state fails closed
- frontier verification does not persist frontier logs

topPRs.title: refactor: move OP EVM code into alloy-op-evm newtypes
topPRs.author: theochap
topPRs.body:
## Summary
- Introduce `OpTx` and `OpTxError` newtype wrappers in alloy-op-evm to hold all OP-specific EVM implementations previously in alloy-evm's `op` module
- Move spec ID mapping and `EvmEnv` constructors as free functions (`evm_env_for_op_block`, `evm_env_for_op_next_block`)
- Add `TryIntoTxEnv<OpTx>` for `OpTransactionRequest` behind `rpc` feature
- Add `TransactionEnv` impl for `OpTx` behind `reth` feature
- Update op-reth, kona, and custom-node example to use new types
- Remove `alloy-evm` `op` feature usage from kona crates

This is the companion PR to https://github.com/alloy-rs/evm/pull/312 which removes the OP-specific code from alloy-evm. Together they decouple alloy-evm from Optimism, using newtype wrappers to satisfy Rust's orphan rule.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p alloy-op-evm` — 24 tests pass

topPRs.title: feat(contracts): add ProxyAdminOwnedBase to L2 proxied contracts with initialize()
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Moves `ProxyAdminOwnedBase` from `src/L1/` to `src/universal/` so it can be used by both L1 and L2 contracts
- Adds `ProxyAdminOwnedBase` inheritance to 7 L2 contracts that have `initialize()` functions, matching the pattern already used by L1 contracts
- Each initializer now calls `_assertOnlyProxyAdminOrProxyAdminOwner()` as its first statement to gate re-initialization behind proxy admin ownership

**Contracts updated (have `initialize()`):**
- `FeeVault` (covers `BaseFeeVault`, `L1FeeVault`, `OperatorFeeVault`, `SequencerFeeVault` transitively)
- `L2CrossDomainMessenger`
- `L2StandardBridge` (covers `L2StandardBridgeInterop` transitively)
- `L2ERC721Bridge`
- `FeeSplitter`
- `LiquidityController`
- `OptimismMintableERC721Factory`

**Contracts intentionally excluded:**
- Contracts without `initialize()` — inheritance would be unused dead code
- `OptimismSuperchainERC20` — BeaconProxy instances, incompatible with `ProxyAdminOwnedBase`

**`L2Genesis.s.sol` changes to support the new assertion:**
- `_setImplementationCode` now calls `EIP1967Helper.setAdmin(impl, Predeploys.PROXY_ADMIN)` so impl addresses pass the `proxyAdmin()` check
- `setPredeployImplementations` pranks as `opChainProxyAdminOwner` so the ownership assertion passes during genesis
- `setL2ProxyAdmin` moved to run first so `proxyAdminOwner()` is set before other contracts' initializers check it

## Test plan

- [ ] `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=lite forge test --match-path "test/L2/*"` — 381 passed, 0 failed, 37 skipped
